comment:
After 30 years you have to pay this much ammount every money  

To calculate the SIP amount after 30 years with a 10% step-up every year, we use the formula for compounded annual growth:

Amount in year n = Initial SIP × (1 + Step-up rate)^(n - 1)

Here:

Initial SIP = 2000

Step-up rate = 10% = 0.10

Duration = 30 years

Let's calculate it:

Amount in year 30 = 2000 × (1 + 0.10)^(30 - 1)
= 2000 × (1.10)^29

Calculating:

1.10 raised to the power of 29 is approximately 15.91.

Thus:
Amount in year 30 = 2000 × 15.91 = 31,820 INR.

After 30 years, the SIP amount will be ₹31,820 per month.

comment:
Fact check: investing ₹10k/month for 30 years totals ₹36 lakh, and ₹2k/month with 10% annual step-up totals ~₹40 lakh. By the final year, the 2k SIP grows to ~₹30k/month (inflation-adjusted ~₹5k), while the 10k SIP would be ~₹10k (~₹2k today). After 30 years, a corpus of ₹7–10 crore adjusts for inflation to ~₹1.2–1.5 crore today.

So even though the 2k step-up SIP starts small, it eventually costs much more in later years, and the difference in total investment is only ~₹20 lakh. Also, part of the invested amount loses value over time due to inflation, so the “real” invested ₹40 lakh is less in today’s terms, yet the final corpus is worth ~₹1.5 crore. It’s not huge, but better to have something than nothing. [edit:- i just calculated the total invested amount after inflation and its insane for 10k its 16lac approx and for 2k its 10 lac approx]

comment:
Hi Akshat!

Thanks for bringing these videos. Here’s a thought for your SIP calculation.

10K for 30 Years = ₹1,20,000 p.a.

Adjusted to 9% inflation:
Value of 1.2L after 10yrs = ₹50,700 p.a.
Value of 1.2L after 20yrs = ₹21,400 p.a.
Value of 1.2L after 30yrs = ₹9,050 p.a.

So the total invested value, adjusted to 9% inflation over 30years = ₹12,45,000.
And not ₹36,00,000.

So, for an investment of ₹12.5L, doesn’t a return of 45-75Lacs seem reasonable?

And yes, there is 1% commission charged under the disguise of Total Expense Ratio but, this is in Regular Plans and not Direct Plans wherein the TER is usually 0.3-0.7% which can bring a difference of good ~₹20Lacs.

The 12% return you’re assuming is XIRR, it already considers the ~1% commission. So, after TER and XIRR, the adjusted corpus will be higher than ₹75Lacs.

Moreover, the LTCG, you’re considering also can be saved by staggering the redemption across various years and a number of other different ways.

Am I missing something?
